title: Mukul Agrawal Adds Seven Stocks, Anchored by a Mining Bet and SME Names
excerpt: September-quarter disclosures so far confirm a 1.33% stake in Tega Industries and a 5.64% entry into Recode Studios, with The Financial Express valuing the mining bet at Rs 189 crore.
body:
• Ace investor Mukul Agrawal appears to have added seven new stocks in the September quarter, according to The Economic Times, with shareholding disclosures still being released.
  • The Financial Express put his largest new bet, in mining, at Rs 189 crore, alongside four newly listed SME stocks.
  • Among the confirmed names: a 5.64% stake in SME-listed Recode Studios, 6,00,000 shares in a beauty company whose stock has risen about 106% in three months, and a 1.33% holding in mining consumables maker Tega Industries.
  • Quarterly shareholding patterns only show holders above disclosure thresholds, so the seven names are a floor, not the full portfolio.

Mukul Agrawal's September-quarter footprint is still emerging, filing by filing. The Economic Times reports the ace investor likely added seven new equity stocks in the second quarter of FY27, with shareholding disclosures still being released and further changes possible. The Financial Express characterised the largest of the new bets as a Rs 189 crore position in mining, alongside four newly listed SME stocks.

Portfolio-watchers track Agrawal because his name in a shareholding pattern has become a signal small-cap investors trade on. The confirmed disclosures so far show the shape of this quarter's version: one mining-linked holding, and a cluster of small, recently listed companies.

The Mining Anchor: Tega Industries

The mining exposure runs through Tega Industries, the Kolkata-based maker of consumables for mineral processing and bulk material handling. Agrawal holds a 1.33% stake in Tega in the September quarter, according to shareholding data reported by Sahi. He had earlier put Rs 100 crore into the company through a preferential raise, subscribing to 5,01,504 shares at Rs 1,994 each alongside Tata and Bandhan mutual funds.

Tega is not a passive holding. With Apollo Global Management, it has made a binding bid for US-based Molycop at an enterprise value of about $1.48 billion, with Tega holding roughly 77% of the acquisition vehicle. An investor buying Tega today is buying that acquisition's execution risk, and its upside, as much as the existing mill-liner business.

The SME Cluster: Recode Studios

The clearest of the newly listed names is Recode Studios, a beauty and personal care company that sells more than 350 products across five categories and was featured on Shark Tank India. Agrawal's name appeared in its September 2026 shareholding pattern with a 5.64% stake, 6,00,000 shares, according to DSIJ.

The stock had risen 105.87% in the three months before the disclosure. Promoters also raised their holding, from 65.02% in May 2026 to 65.18% in September, and management has guided for at least 50% growth in FY27, backed by wider distribution and a Ludhiana warehouse expected to operate from April 2027. A 5.64% stake is not a toe in the water; in an SME-listed company, it makes Agrawal one of the largest public shareholders.

How to Read a Pattern Like This

Two cautions belong in every story built on shareholding patterns. First, the patterns are backward-looking snapshots of a quarter that ended weeks before publication; positions may already have changed. Second, disclosure thresholds mean a pattern shows only holders above 1% in most cases, so an investor can hold a meaningful position invisibly, and can also exit below the threshold without any filing saying so.

That is why the honest summary of Agrawal's quarter, so far, is a direction rather than a list: toward mining-linked industrials with global ambitions, and toward very small, very young listed companies where a single large holder can move both the register and the price.

What's Next

More September-quarter patterns will land over the coming days, and each one can add a name to, or quietly remove one from, the Agrawal watchlist. The full picture of the seven new positions will only be settled when the disclosure season closes.
